newsitem.title: HAITI: Former politician killed in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: Former politician killed in Haiti.

text.p: A conservative politician who was a member of Haiti's parliament during its three-year military dictatorship was shot and killed on a busy Port-au-Prince street Thursday, according to local politicians and an independent radio report.

Dates Milsunt, a former member of the Chamber of Deputies from northern Haiti, was shot twice by two armed men as he stepped out of his car to buy groceries. The two men then stole his car, Signal FM radio said.
In August 1991, Milsunt called for a no-confidence vote against Rene Preval, who was then prime minister under former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide and is now president.

The vote was unsuccessful but Aristide and Preval were ousted from power and forced into exile two months later. Aristide was returned to the presidency in 1994. Preval was elected president, succeeding Aristide, in December 1995.
Police said they could provide no information about the killing. Members of parliament who knew Milsunt confirmed that he had been gunned down.

There was no indication the killing was politically motivated. Haiti's capital has been rocked by violent crime this year, and this has prompted concern about the competence of its police as a July 31 deadline approaches for the withdrawal of U.N. peacekeeping troops.
